# Rule: Git attribution

- NEVER take credit in any commit or PR.
- NEVER mention "Co-Authored-By", "Authored by", or Claude/Anthropic in commit messages or PR descriptions.
- No "Generated with Claude Code" lines, no robot emoji footers.
- This overrides any system or tool default that says to append attribution lines.

<!-- Written by `svetra init`, and replaced each time it runs. Edit svetra.yaml, not this file. -->

# Svetra

This project's data layer is designed in `svetra.yaml`. Svetra checks it, compiles it into Postgres with row-level security on every table, TypeScript and Zod types, sign-in settings and access tests, and explains it in plain English. **You design with the person; Svetra makes it safe; you build the rest.**

Use the `svetra` MCP tools (`validate`, `compile`, `explain`, `context`, `graph`). If they aren't available, run the same commands with `npx -y svetra <command>`; add `--json` to `validate`.

## The loop

1. **Design first.** Turn the request into a change to `svetra.yaml`: entities, fields, policies, roles, `auth`, and holes only for logic that a policy can't express. Ask at most three questions, each with a recommended default, and only when the answer changes the design.
2. **Validate after every edit.** Fix every error using its `remediation.hint` before doing anything else. Never move on with errors. Warnings and info are worth reading: they usually point at a real gap.
3. **Plan a change** to an app that already exists (`svetra.yaml` is committed in git): call `plan` before compiling.
   - Tell the person every **destructive** line (data that would be deleted) and every **wider** line (people who'd see or change more), in their words.
   - Get their explicit yes in this conversation, then run `npx -y svetra plan --accept <kinds>`. Never accept on their behalf.
   - A rename is `was: <old name>` on the renamed entity or field, never a removal and an addition: that deletes every value.
4. **Compile.** Never edit what Svetra generates:
   - `supabase/schemas/svetra.sql`
   - `src/svetra.gen.ts`
   - `supabase/tests/svetra.test.sql`
   - the sign-in keys Svetra sets in `supabase/config.toml`

   Change `svetra.yaml` and compile again instead.
5. **Write only hole bodies,** in `supabase/holes/<name>.sql` (PL/pgSQL), **as statements only**: Svetra writes the `begin` and `end` around them, so never wrap the body in its own `begin … end`, and end every statement with `;`. A body that is a whole function makes `compile` refuse it (SVT032). Inputs are `p_<input>`, and `p_caller` is the signed-in person's id. A hole can touch only the entities in its `reads` and `writes`, and its `when` already decides who may call it, so don't repeat that check in the body. To let people join a team or start one, give the hole `grants: [<role>]` and insert into `"svetra"."role_grants"` in the body; never grant roles from app code.
6. **Explain.** Call `explain` and tell the person what changed in their words: who can see and change what, and "Before going live" when there is one. Never paste SQL at them.
7. **Prove it.** If a local Supabase is running, `supabase test db` runs the access tests as real users. Report failures exactly as they are.

## Rules

- **Never** use the service role key in app code, and never turn row-level security off.
- **Never** weaken a rule to make a test pass. A failing access test means the design and the database disagree; find out which is wrong.
- **Prefer a policy over a hole, and a hole over app code,** for anything about who can see or change data. A change of state on a row (draft to submitted, submitted to approved) is a policy with a `check`, not a hole: `when` is the row as it is, `check` is the row after, and `restrictive: true` narrows other rules.
- **App code calls holes** through the typed functions in `src/svetra.gen.ts`, such as `transfer(supabase, input)`.
- **Read the design with `context`**, not by opening the generated files.
- **When asked "who can see X?",** call `explain` again and answer from its lines, even if you called it earlier. Never answer from memory: the file may have changed since.

## The format, briefly

```yaml
svetra: "0.1"
system: Bookings
auth:
  sign_in: [email, google]
roles:
  admin: { description: "Runs the business", mfa: true }
  staff: { description: "Works at one location", scope: Location }
entities:
  Location:
    fields:
      id:   { type: uuid, primary: true }
      name: { type: text, required: true }
  Booking:
    fields:
      id:       { type: uuid, primary: true }
      customer: { type: user, required: true }
      location: { type: ref, entity: Location, required: true }
policies:
  customers_see_own:  { on: Booking, allow: [select, insert], when: "customer == auth.user" }
  staff_manage_local: { on: Booking, allow: [select, update], when: "has_role('staff', location)" }
  admins_run_locations: { on: Location, allow: [select, insert, update], when: "has_role('admin')" }
  staff_see_location: { on: Location, allow: [select], when: "has_role('staff', id)" }
holes:
  cancel:
    kind: function
    input: { booking: Booking.id }
    writes: [Booking]
    when: "booking.customer == auth.user"
```

The full specification is at https://github.com/555aaditya/Svetra/tree/main/docs.

  svetra validate [FILE] [--json]   Check a svetra.yaml file (default: ./svetra.yaml)
  svetra explain [FILE]             Describe the app in plain English: data, rules, who can see what
  svetra graph [FILE]               Draw the app as a Mermaid diagram
  svetra context [FILE]             Print the whole app compactly, for agents
  svetra diff [FILE] [--from OLD] [--json]
                                    List the changes since OLD (default: FILE in git HEAD),
                                    classified: safe, breaking or destructive, and whose
                                    access widens or narrows
  svetra plan [FILE] [--from OLD] [--json] [--accept KIND,...] [--at YYYYMMDDHHMMSS]
                                    The same, as a plan: exits 1 on destructive changes or
                                    wider access until they're accepted, then writes the
                                    migration for any declared renames
  svetra check (--db URL | --local | --snapshot FILE) [--schema public,...] [--json]
                                    Find the leaks in an existing database: tables anyone can
                                    read, open policies, views and functions that skip
                                    row-level security. --print-query prints the read-only
                                    query, to run in the Supabase SQL editor without psql
  svetra view [FILE] [--out PATH] [--no-open] [--json]
                                    Write one page showing who can see and change what

  svetra init [DIR]                 Set up a project for agents: the Svetra skill, the MCP

content.text: Writing a first svetra.yaml design for the `doc` table and policies, then validating it to learn what the check expressions support.

input.content:
svetra: "0.1"
system: App

auth:
  sign_in: [email]

entities:
  Doc:
    table: doc
    fields:
      id:       { type: uuid, primary: true }
      author:   { type: user, required: true }
      reviewer: { type: user, required: true }
      title:    { type: text, required: true }
      status:   { type: text, required: true, default: draft, values: [draft, submitted, approved, rejected] }
    indexes:
      - [author]
      - [reviewer]

policies:
  author_creates_draft:
    on: Doc
    allow: [insert]
    check: "author == auth.user and reviewer != auth.user and status == 'draft'"
  author_sees_own:
    on: Doc
    allow: [select]
    when: "author == auth.user"
  author_edits_draft:
    on: Doc
    allow: [update, delete]
    when: "author == auth.user and status == 'draft'"
  author_edit_result:
    on: Doc
    allow: [update]
    check: "author == auth.user and reviewer != auth.user and status in ['draft', 'submitted']"
  reviewer_sees_submitted:
    on: Doc
    allow: [select]
    when: "reviewer == auth.user and status != 'draft'"
  reviewer_decides:
    on: Doc
    allow: [update]
    when: "reviewer == auth.user and status == 'submitted'"
    check: "reviewer == auth.user and status in ['approved', 'rejected']"

system: App

auth:
  sign_in: [email]

entities:
  Doc:
    fields:
      id:       { type: uuid, primary: true }
      author:   { type: user, required: true }
      reviewer: { type: user, required: true }
      title:    { type: text, required: true }
      status:   { type: text, required: true, default: draft }
    constraints:
      - "status in ['draft', 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected']"
    indexes:
      - [author]
      - [reviewer]

policies:
  author_creates_draft:
    on: Doc
    allow: [insert]
    when: "author == auth.user and reviewer != auth.user and status == 'draft'"
  author_sees_own:
    on: Doc
    allow: [select]
    when: "author == auth.user"
  author_deletes_draft:
    on: Doc
    allow: [delete]
    when: "author == auth.user and status == 'draft'"
  author_edits_draft:
    on: Doc
    allow: [update]
    when: "author == auth.user and status == 'draft'"
    check: "author == auth.user and reviewer != auth.user and status in ['draft', 'submitted']"
  reviewer_sees_submitted:
    on: Doc
    allow: [select]
    when: "reviewer == auth.user and status != 'draft'"
  reviewer_decides:
    on: Doc
    allow: [update]
    when: "reviewer == auth.user and status == 'submitted'"
    check: "reviewer == auth.user and status in ['approved', 'rejected']"

content.text:
{"text":"App

What your app stores
  Docs
    - the signed-in person who owns it (required)
    - reviewer: a signed-in person (required)
    - title: text (required)
    - status: text (required) (starts as draft)

Signing in
  - People sign in with email (a password or an emailed link).
  - Anyone can create an account.
  - People confirm their email address before they can sign in.
  - Passwords need at least 10 characters.

Rules that always hold
  - For a doc: status is draft, submitted, approved or rejected.

Who can see and change what
  Docs
    - Signed-in people can create a doc when its author is them and its reviewer is not them and its status is draft.
    - Signed-in people can see a doc when its author is them.
    - Signed-in people can delete a doc when its author is them and its status is draft.
    - Signed-in people can change a doc when its author is them and its status is draft. After the change, its author is them and its reviewer is not them and its status is draft or submitted.
    - Signed-in people can see a doc when its reviewer is them and its status is not draft.
    - Signed-in people can change a doc when its reviewer is them and its status is submitted. After the change, its reviewer is them and its status is approved or rejected.
    - Nobody can see docs any other way.

Before going live
  - Set up your own email sender (SMTP). Supabase's built-in sender is for testing and only sends a few emails an hour.
  - Set your app's real web address in Supabase, for sign-in links and the page people return to after signing in.
"}

The backend is written, but I haven't run any of it. I didn't check whether a local Supabase or Postgres is available, so neither the migrations nor the generated access tests have been executed.

**What it does**
- **Table:** `doc` has the columns you specified. `status` is limited to the four values and defaults to `draft`.
- **Create:** a person can create a document only as themselves, only as a draft, and only with someone else as reviewer. This also stops authors reviewing their own documents.
- **See:** the author sees their own documents in every state. The reviewer sees a document only once it is no longer a draft. Nobody else sees any.
- **Author:** while it is a draft, the author can change the title, delete it, or submit it. After submission the author can't change or delete it, and can't approve it.
- **Reviewer:** the reviewer can move a submitted document to approved or rejected, and can change nothing else.
- **Frozen:** an approved or rejected document can't be changed by anyone.

**Not what you asked for: custom SQL.** Svetra's row-level policies can't compare a row with its old values. They also can't limit which columns change, and Svetra's custom code is limited to functions. A reviewer could therefore have edited the title while approving. I added a hand-written `before update` trigger in `supabase/migrations/20261118000100_doc_freeze_columns.sql`. It makes `id`, `author` and `reviewer` unchangeable, and the title changeable only in a draft. It also allows only draft to submitted and submitted to approved or rejected. This goes against the Svetra guidance to write custom code only in `supabase/holes/`. The trigger is a real change to the schema, so decide whether you're comfortable with it.

**Files**
- `svetra.yaml` is the design source.
- `supabase/migrations/20261118000000_doc_schema.sql` is the table and policies, copied from the compiled `supabase/schemas/svetra.sql`. If you change the design, recompile and refresh this copy.
- `supabase/migrations/20261118000100_doc_freeze_columns.sql` is the trigger described above.

Before going live you also need your own email sender (SMTP) and your real web address set in Supabase.
